articles.title: Compra da Warner Bros. pela Paramount cria gigante com 200 milhões de assinantes; veja os números | G1
articles.standfirst: Acordo foi concluído nesta terça-feira (6) e cria a Skydance, que será dona de franquias como 'Harry Potter', 'Game of Thrones' e 'Batman'.
articles.summary: Acordo foi concluído nesta terça-feira (6) e cria a Skydance, que será dona de franquias como 'Harry Potter', 'Game of Thrones' e 'Batman'.
articles.body:
Foto ilustrativa mostra logotipos da Paramount e da Warner Bros — Foto: Reuters

Com o anúncio da Paramount Skydance nesta terça-feira (6) sobre a conclusão da compra da Warner Bros. Discovery , as empresas formarão uma gigante capaz de alcançar 200 milhões de assinantes.

A fusão criará a empresa Skydance, que será dona de marcas como Warner Bros., Paramount Pictures, HBO, CNN, CBS, além dos serviços de streaming Paramount+ e HBO Max. No catálogo, há franquias como "Harry Potter" e "Game of Thrones", "Batman", "Missão: Impossível" e "Top Gun".

O grupo será comandado por David Ellison, filho do bilionário Larry Ellison, cofundador da Oracle – os dois já controlam a Paramount Skydance. Ynon Kreiz, ex-CEO da Mattel, será co-CEO e responsável pelas operações da nova empresa.

O acordo avaliado em US$ 110 bilhões encerra uma das maiores disputas recentes pelo controle de ativos em Hollywood. A venda da Warner Bros. era negociada desde 2025 e envolveu a concorrência de empresas como a Netflix, que chegou a oferecer US$ 83 bilhões.

A criação da Skydance tem o potencial de redesenhar o mercado do entretenimento e do streaming em todo o mundo. O g1 preparou um infográfico que compara o tamanho das empresas e mostra como a operação pode alterar o equilíbrio de forças no setor.

Veja os números da junção entre Warner e Paramount — Foto: Arte/g1

Em dezembro de 2025, a Netflix anunciou um acordo de US$ 83 bilhões para comprar parte dos ativos da Warner Bros. Discovery , com foco nos negócios de estúdio e streaming, sendo US$ 72 bilhões para acionistas e o restante para o pagamento de dívidas.

Depois, a Paramount Skydance entrou na negociação com uma proposta concorrente para adquirir a empresa inteira, incluindo os canais tradicionais.

Em fevereiro de 2026, a Warner informou que a Paramount tinha aumentado a proposta para os US$ 110 bilhões , voltados a acionistas e dívidas, e se comprometido a pagar uma multa de US$ 2,8 bilhões pela desistência do acordo com a Netflix.

A Netflix teria quatro dias para apresentar uma contraproposta , mas decidiu abandonar a disputa por considerar que, com a oferta da Paramount, "o acordo deixou de ser financeiramente atraente".

O impacto da operação vai além do valor bilionário. A Warner Bros. Discovery detém algumas das marcas mais valiosas da indústria do entretenimento, enquanto a Paramount busca ganhar escala para competir com gigantes como Netflix e Disney.

💰 A compra pela Paramount envolve todo o grupo Warner Bros. Discovery , enquanto a oferta da Netflix excluía ativos como CNN e Discovery.

🗞️ Com a conclusão do acordo, a família Ellison, aliada do presidente americano Donald Trump, passa a controlar algumas das principais marcas do jornalismo nos EUA , como a CBS News, o programa 60 Minutes e a CNN.

📺 A Paramount também ampliará sua base de assinantes e fortalecerá sua presença em cinema, TV e plataformas digitais .

articles.title: Após fim de prazo para saques de recursos nas bets, contas de apostadores ainda têm R$ 1,32 bilhão | G1
articles.standfirst: Valores serão enviados a bancos, que, entre os dias 9 e 14, deverão devolver quantias a apostadores. Caixa Econômica Federal vai intermediar a devolução nos casos em que houver algum impedimento.
articles.summary: Valores serão enviados a bancos, que, entre os dias 9 e 14, deverão devolver quantias a apostadores. Caixa Econômica Federal vai intermediar a devolução nos casos em que houver algum impedimento.
articles.body:
O Ministério da Fazenda informou nesta terça-feira (6) que as contas de 26,5 milhões de apostadores nas bets ainda reúnem R$ 1,32 bilhão. O prazo para saque dos recursos das plataformas de apostas se encerrou nesta segunda-feira (5).

A proibição das bets foi anunciada pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva em 25 de setembro . A vedação inclui também jogos online e cassinos virtuais no país, como por exemplo, o "Jogo do Tigrinho".

🔎Lula também enviou ao Congresso um projeto de lei que estabelece penas para quem explorar, operar ou divulgar as bets e os cassinos virtuais. Ao tomar as medidas, o petista mencionou o endividamento de famílias e o vício de apostadores em jogos de azar.

➡️ A partir desta terça-feira (6), os sites e aplicativos das plataformas de apostas estão indisponíveis. Segundo o governo, quem tentar acessar as plataformas será redirecionado para uma página com orientações sobre o resgate dos valores e as garantias de devolução dos recursos.

"De ontem para hoje, houve uma diminuição de cerca de R$ 5 milhões nos recursos, passando para R$ 1,325 bilhão na terça-feira (6). Um dos aspectos que podem estar relacionados ao ritmo de retirada dos recursos é a quantidade de contas com valores reduzidos. Ao todo, 86,2 milhões de contas possuem saldos entre R$ 0,01 e R$ 0,99, que, somados, representam R$ 15,5 milhões", informou o Ministério da Fazenda.

Com o fim do prazo de saque, as empresas terão até quarta-feira (7) para encaminhar às instituições financeiras os saldos remanescentes de cada apostador, discriminados por CPF, além da conta bancária utilizada para os depósitos.

Entre sexta-feira (9) e a próxima quarta-feira (14), as instituições financeiras deverão realizar a devolução dos valores aos apostadores.

A partir de 14 de outubro, a Caixa Econômica Federal passará a intermediar a devolução nos casos em que houver algum impedimento.

Quase 700 bets ilegais foram criadas depois da proibição anunciada pelo governo, aponta levantamento — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

De acordo com o Ministério da Fazenda, governo federal já adotou providências para derrubar mais de 11 mil sites ilegais de apostas online em uma semana de vigência da medida provisória do presidente Lula derrubou as bets no país.

Ao todo, foram derrubados 11.056 sites nesse período, sendo 1.600 somente nesta terça-feira (6), quando os sites e aplicativos das plataformas de apostas passaram a ficar indisponíveis.

Antes da publicação da MP, outros 78 mil sites ilegais já haviam sido derrubados pela Anatel a pedido do Executivo.

articles.title: Karnataka expands GIA to drive tech outcomes
articles.summary: Karnataka expands Global Innovation Alliance to focus on joint tech development, startup market access, research and investments ahead of Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026.
articles.body: Bengaluru: Karnataka is looking to turn its global technology partnerships into concrete outcomes, with its Global Innovation Alliance (GIA) initiative focusing on joint technology development, startup market access, research and investments rather than MoUs and delegations.Speaking at a GIA meeting in Bengaluru, IT minister Priyank Kharge said the initiative would focus on converting international engagements into measurable outcomes.“GIA is about moving from engagement to execution, from MoUs to outcomes, and from delegations to enduring partnerships. Ecosystem-to-ecosystem relationships will always outlast individual transactions,” he said.The meeting was held ahead of Bengaluru Tech Summit (BTS) 2026, scheduled from Nov 17-19.“Under GIA, success will not be measured by the number of delegations or MoUs alone, but by how many startups enter new markets, how many technologies are jointly developed, how many research programmes are launched, how many pilots become businesses, and how many investments and jobs are created,” Kharge said.The GIA network, launched in 2017, has grown from 10 countries in 2018 to more than 40 partner countries in 2026, with Karnataka engaging with over 90 countries globally.The initiative will focus on four areas — startup mobility and market access, institutional partnerships, global visibility and strategic engagement, and governance through a dedicated international desk.Karnataka is also developing the Global Innovation and Growth Alliance (GIGA), a physical collaboration space in Bengaluru for international startups, innovation agencies and institutions.The summit, themed ‘AI & Beyond’, is expected to draw more than 90,000 attendees, 25,000 delegates, 1,000 startups, 1,000 investors, 700 speakers and 1,800 exhibitors from more than 75 countries.You use AI every day. articles.title: Paramount closes $110 billion deal with Warner Brothers Discovery: The new company is called Skydance
articles.summary: The entity Skydance will be led by tech scion David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz, formerly the top executive at Mattel. Paramount's purchase of Warner Bros.
articles.body: The entity Skydance will be led by tech scion David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz, formerly the top executive at Mattel.Paramount's purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, which Hollywood spent most of 2026 treating as either inevitable or illegal, depending on who was paying for the lunch, is done. The parent company will be called Skydance, and David Ellison will run it alongside his incoming co-CEO Ynon Kreiz. Ellison simply reused the name of Skydance Media, his original film production company, as the umbrella for everything being folded into the new conglomerate. Paramount and Warner Bros. themselves survive as brands under that umbrella, keeping their logos on their films, much as Universal sits under Comcast.The road here was not short. Paramount offered $31 a share in cash, valuing Warner's equity at $81 billion and the whole transaction at $110 billion once debt is counted. Netflix had got there first, with a $27.75-a-share agreement for the studio and streaming assets, but when the price rose its co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters told Warner the deal was no longer financially attractive and walked away. Then came a lawsuit from twelve states. On September 30, U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín approved Paramount's settlement with them, and the price of that settlement is worth reading closely. The combined company must release at least 30 theatrical films a year for two years and 32 for the following three, pay a $30 million penalty for every film it falls short, and honour 45-day theatrical windows. It must also set up an independent editorial board to oversee CNN and CBS News. Rarely has a merger been approved on the condition that it behave like two companies.Which brings us to Kreiz, the most interesting hire in Hollywood this year. At Mattel since 2018, he turned toy brands into films, TV shows and games, and delivered "Barbie," the highest-grossing film Warner Bros. has ever had. The man who rented Warner its biggest hit now gets the keys to the building. He will oversee daily operations and the combined businesses, while Ellison leads strategy, creative and technology. Ellison, in short, keeps the vision and hands Kreiz the spreadsheet.That spreadsheet is not a gentle one. Paramount is aiming for more than $6 billion in savings from the merger, and Kreiz's turnaround at Mattel included job cuts. To fund the purchase, Paramount is issuing about $42.4 billion in bonds and taking out a further $8.5 billion and €850 million in loans. Three Middle Eastern funds will own 38.5% of the merged company, according to Paramount. The leadership reshuffle has already begun: Warner Bros. Pictures chiefs Michael De Luca and Pamela Abdy will not be part of Ellison's team.Ellison describes Skydance as "a creative-first home for bold, quality storytelling." The settlement, with its film quotas and per-title fines, suggests that twelve state attorneys general were not entirely prepared to take his word for it.(With wire inputs)You use AI every day. articles.title: Lush expands India presence, plans 30 stores in five years
articles.summary: Lush to expand in India with 30 stores in five years, up from its 10-year plan; aims for 8 stores by FY27 and grows Bengaluru local production.
articles.body: BENGALURU: To Rowena Bird, India looks very different from the market Lush first entered years ago. The 1995-founded British cosmetics brand, whose founders created the bath bomb, had arrived before premium beauty had really taken off here. Malls were fewer. Imported brands were less familiar. Even Lush’s unpackaged soaps and fizzing bath bombs often needed explaining.This time, Bird believes the market is ready.“The market has very much changed,” the Lush co-founder told TOI. “There are a lot more Western brands... people are open to looking at something new.”Bird said Lush’s mistake the first time was entering too early. Import taxes were high and the market for premium cosmetics was still developing. “I don’t think the market was really ready for us,” she said.The shift is encouraging Lush to move faster in India. Its original business plan envisaged 30 stores over 10 years. It projected annual sales of around £11 million at that scale. The India team now believes it could reach the store target in about five years.Lush currently has five stores in the country. It expects to have eight in FY27 and is forecasting India sales of just under £2 million for the year. Ahmedabad, Jaipur and Hyderabad are next on its expansion map. Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru are expected to eventually have multiple stores.“We are already, in terms of number of stores, doing more than our plan,” said Vishal Anand, who leads Lush’s India business. “I think we should be able to achieve that plan in five years.”Bird said India is currently performing slightly better than Lush had projected. Even at the planned 30-store scale, however, the country would be a medium-sized market for the company. Lush operates across about 55 markets.Local manufacturing is also increasing. Lush currently makes six products at its Bengaluru “fresh kitchen”. These already account for about 6% of India sales. The company plans to increase the locally made range to 30 products, largely across fresh face packs, hair masks, eye pads and cleansers.The Bengaluru unit has enough capacity to support as many as 50 stores. But Lush does not expect to manufacture its entire portfolio in India. Much of the wider assortment will continue to be imported.Indian customers have also challenged some of Lush’s early assumptions. Shower products account for about 26% of sales and haircare about 23%. Bath bombs, which the company thought could be a harder sell in India, have also performed better than expected.Customers typically buy more than two products per transaction, the company said. Repeat purchases are also rising as stores mature. Online purchases currently account for about 29% of its India sales.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Sarvam AI appoints Ex-Google Cloud India MD  Sreedharan as president
articles.summary: Sarvam AI hires ex-Google Cloud India MD Sashikumar Sreedharan as president and CBO, boosting its sovereign AI model and infrastructure ambitions in India.
articles.body: Bengaluru: In its first high-profile C-suite hire, homegrown AI unicorn Sarvam AI has roped in former Google Cloud India MD Sashikumar Sreedharan as president and chief business officer, sources told TOI.Sreedharan recently stepped down from Google Cloud and is currently serving his garden leave period. Amit Kumar, managing director of Digital Natives Business at Google Cloud India, has been appointed interim MD, succeeding him.The appointment comes as Sarvam is building out its leadership bench and research capabilities even as it doubles down on its ambition to develop sovereign AI infrastructure and models in India. An email sent to Sarvam did not elicit a response till press time.The homegrown AI startup recently appointed AI researcher Devendra Chaplot, a founding member of Mistral AI and Thinking Machine Labs, as an adviser. California-based Chaplot is part of Sarvam’s efforts to tap global Indian AI talent.Sreedharan brings experience in building cloud businesses for enterprises and the public sector. At Google Cloud, he led the expansion of its sovereign cloud capabilities in India, catering to organisations with stringent requirements around data security, control and isolation. He was previously managing director of Microsoft India and CEO and MD of Happiest Minds.Sarvam’s leadership expansion follows a $234 million funding round led by HCLTech and Bessemer Venture Partners that valued the company at $1.5 billion, making it one of India’s newest AI unicorns. The Bengaluru-based startup’s revenue was Rs 45 crore in FY26, according to unaudited financials.The company is now planning to build a trillion-parameter AI model and establish a US office to attract Indian-origin AI researchers. At the company’s recent flagship event, its founder Pratyush Kumar told TOI the model will target capabilities in coding, cybersecurity, scientific research and simulation, bringing Sarvam closer to the frontier of global AI models.The company’s current 100-billion-parameter model is already being used for voice AI, conversational systems, English speech recognition and dictation, besides more complex tasks, Kumar said in a recent interaction with TOI. Sarvam has so far processed 325 million minutes of voice calls, he told TOI.“India should be producing the AI tokens it consumes,” Kumar told TOI, arguing that continued dependence on overseas models could leave India paying not only for access to AI but also through the data generated by its users.Raghavan said Sarvam wants to build a “real token factory in India”. Serving AI tokens from within the country, he said, would be “the first step to becoming sovereign”.The company also believes sovereignty cannot come at the cost of performance. “Sovereignty should not be a tax,” Kumar said, arguing that Indian AI products must be benchmarked against the best global models rather than getting a pass simply because they are homegrown.Sarvam is already building its model portfolio. Its latest speech recognition model, Saaras V4, combines an audio encoder with a 3-billion-parameter hybrid state-space model decoder, trained entirely in-house from scratch.Sarvam said Saaras V4 delivers state-of-the-art performance across all 22 Indian languages, including low-resource languages. It also records the lowest word error rate across seven global English datasets, covering six non-native English dialects and Indian English.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient.
